comments.author: arogozhnikov
comments.body:
Hi Luke,

> I was surprised that einops.reduce and einops.rearrange does not handle this case. 

```
einops.reduce('b c h w -> b c') averages over h w
einsum('b c n n -> b c') averages over trace. 
```
If reduce supported this logic, a ton of code out there would be incorrect (because - yes - in many cases you want to name same-size dims with same label). So it's simply not allowed.

> Adding this as a feature will also help einops become feature complete with np.einsum.

there is einops.einsum, and this is one of reasons for its existence.

comments.author: lukemarris
comments.body:
> If reduce supported this logic, a ton of code out there would be incorrect (because - yes - in many cases you want to name same-size dims with same label). So it's simply not allowed.

For future readers, I was under the impression duplicate entries always raised an exception so it would be safe to add this feature. However I was mistaken. It seems duplicate entries are permitted with the `allow_duplicates` argument. So Alex is right that this feature would break backwards compatibility. 

```
if not (allow_underscore and x == "_") and not allow_duplicates:
    raise EinopsError('Indexing expression contains duplicate dimension "{}"'.format(x))
```
From: https://github.com/arogozhnikov/einops/blob/1d3f9c48047ba147211c8f15a079db8e87766a0b/einops/parsing.py#L53
